newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA BULBANK POSTS 12.4 BLN LEV '96 NET PROFIT.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA BULBANK POSTS 12.4 BLN LEV '96 NET PROFIT.

text.p: Bulgaria's Bulbank (Bulgarian Foreign Trade Bank) posted 12.4 billion lev net profit for 1996, up from 788 million levs for 1995, the bank's chief excutive director said on Thursday.
"The bank had 12.4 billion lev net profit last year. We would use 10.083 billion levs of the net to raise the bank's capital," Chavdar Kanchev told a news conference.
The annual shareholders' meeting due on April 17 is expected to approve a capital rise to 15.124 billion levs from 5.041 billion levs through a new share issue to be backed by the 1996 net.
Only current shareholders would be entitled to two shares from the new issue for each share they hold now.
The Bank Consolidation Company (BCC), which manages state equity in local commercial banks, holds 98.03 percent of Bulbank.
Instead of distributing dividend for last year Bulbank will pay 15 percent profit tax or 1.5 billion levs from the net for its shareholders after they acquire shares from the new issue, Kanchev said.
The remaining 793 million levs of the net would be transferred to the bank's reserves.
Bulbank's pre-tax profit for last year amounted to 185.7 billion levs, from which the bank set aside provisions against risk assets of 163.9 billion levs and paid 9.6 billion levs in taxes.
The bank plans to change name to Bulbank Ltd. from Bulbank (Bulgarian Foreign Trade Bank) Ltd. at the shareholders' meeting.
"This is to indicate to the international financial community that the period of narrow-field performance is over and now the bank is operating as an universal bank," Kanchev said.
Bulbank is considered the biggest Bulgarian commercial bank with assets totalling 1.35 trillion levs ($2.769 billion) at the end of 1996. -- Roumiana Tikholova, Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
